newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up after SBI's dlr demand is met.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up after SBI's dlr demand is met.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up on Wednesday at 35.8150/8200 against the dollar after touching a low of 35.84 during the day, dealers said.
"There was little demand except from SBI (State Bank of India)," said a dealer at a state-run bank. The rupee revived to the 35.82 level as SBI's demand tapered off, he said.
Most of the day's deals were at 35.8250, dealers said.
"There were some (dollar) sellers towards the end of day but this was not the major factor," said another dealer.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) did not intervene.
Some dealers said the usual month-end spurt in dollar demand appeared to have been met.
"I don't see much demand now," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "I see more dollar supplies in the coming days."
The forward dollar market did not see much action except for some institutional purchases for October/November months early on Wednesday, dealers said.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed at 4.75 percent compared with the previous close of 4.64 percent.
